{{short description|Canadian biologist}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2019}}

'''Nicole Buckley''' (born 1960) is a Canadian biologist.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pf7CDgAAQBAJ&q=Buckley&pg=PT171|title=A Galaxy of Her Own: Amazing Stories of Women in Space|last=Jackson|first=Libby|date=2017-11-16|publisher=Random House|isbn=9781473553262|language=en}}</ref> Buckley was the Chief Scientist for Life Sciences and [[International Space Station|ISS]] Utilization at the [[Canadian Space Agency]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/humans/nicole-buckley.asp|title=Humans of the CSA - Nicole Buckley - Chief Scientist, Life Sciences and ISS Utilization|date=2016-03-29|website=www.asc-csa.gc.ca|access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pf7CDgAAQBAJ&q=Buckley&pg=PT171|title=A Galaxy of Her Own: Amazing Stories of Women in Space|last=Jackson|first=Libby|date=2017-11-16|publisher=Random House|isbn=9781473553262|language=en}}</ref> Appointed to the role in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cihr-irsc.gc.ca/e/50739.html|title=IA Institute Advisory Board Members – Biographies - CIHR|last=Government of Canada|first=Canadian Institutes of Health Research|date=2003-04-30|website=www.cihr-irsc.gc.ca|access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref> she worked to highlight the benefits of space science for all, particularly in regard to research on ageing in space.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Thumm|first1=Tracy|last2=Robinson|first2=Julie A.|last3=Alleyne|first3=Camille|last4=Hasbrook|first4=Pete|last5=Mayo|first5=Susan|last6=Buckley|first6=Nicole|last7=Johnson-Green|first7=Perry|last8=Karabadzhak|first8=George|last9=Kamigaichi|first9=Shigeki|last10=Umemura|first10=Sayaka|last11=Sorokin|first11=Igor V.|date=2014-10-01|title=International space station accomplishments update: Scientific discovery, advancing future exploration, and benefits brought home to earth|journal=Acta Astronautica|volume=103|pages=235–242|doi=10.1016/j.actaastro.2014.06.017|bibcode=2014AcAau.103..235T |issn=0094-5765|hdl=2060/20140002474|s2cid=108517267 |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Payne |first1=Elizabeth |title=What astronauts can teach us about aging |url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/local-news/what-astronauts-can-teach-us-about-aging |access-date=November 6, 2019 |work=Ottawa Citizen |date=November 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107044243/https://ottawacitizen.com/news/local-news/what-astronauts-can-teach-us-about-aging/ |archive-date=November 7, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her current position is Team Leader for the SciSpacE team at the European Space Agency (ESA).

Buckley studied Microbiology at the [[University of Saskatchewan]], where she received her bachelor's and master's degree.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://seds.ca/ascension2019/|title=Ascension 2019 – SEDS Canada|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-10}}</ref> She received her PhD in Oral Biology from the [[University of Manitoba]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Buckley|first=Nicole Denyse|date=1993|title=Glucose transport by Streptococcus mutans|url=https://mspace.lib.umanitoba.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/1993/17555/Buckley_Glucose_Transport.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220414153619/https://mspace.lib.umanitoba.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/1993/17555/Buckley_Glucose_Transport.pdf |archive-date=2022-04-14 |url-status=live}}</ref>
